steps.name: QC, filtering, and DESeq2 dataset construction
caveats: Do not filter on statistics computed before size-factor estimation (e.g. raw total counts) in a way that could bias downstream tests; standard practice is filtering on raw count thresholds, which is what is used here.
If metadata sample identifiers do not match counts column names exactly (case, ordering, extra characters), fix the join explicitly rather than assuming positional alignment.
steps.question: Are the 24 samples (2 conditions x t0-t3 x 3 replicates) balanced and free of confounding batch structure, and which of the 12000 genes have sufficient counts to test?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 QC/filtering/PCA workflow ahead of an LRT design; Love/Huber/Anders 2014 (PMID 25516281) documents the recommended pre-filtering and size-factor estimation this step follows.

acceptance_criteria: counts.csv (12000 genes x 25 columns: gene symbol + 24 samples) and metadata.csv (24 samples x condition/time/time_hours/id) are loaded and sample IDs are matched/ordered identically between the two files
time is coded as an ordered 4-level factor (t0,t1,t2,t3) and condition as a 2-level factor; the 2x4x3 cross-tabulation is confirmed balanced (3 per cell)
low-count genes are filtered (e.g. require count >=10 in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size) before DESeq2 size-factor estimation
a VST-based PCA and a sample-correlation heatmap are produced, colored/labeled by condition and time, to flag any outlier sample or batch-like structure before modeling
a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition + time + condition:time and estimated size factors is saved for downstream steps

steps.name: Condition:time interaction test (LRT)
caveats: The interaction term has 3 degrees of freedom here (4 time levels x 2 conditions coding), so the LRT statistic is an omnibus test of any deviation from parallel trajectories, not a single-direction fold change; do not report a single log2FoldChange as if it summarized the whole test.
If zero or very few genes pass padj<0.05, report that plainly rather than lowering the threshold post hoc without saying so.
steps.question: Which genes have a significant condition x time interaction (full model ~condition+time+condition:time vs reduced model ~condition+time), i.e. a treatment-specific trajectory beyond the shared time trend?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 LRT with reduced model dropping the interaction term is the standard approach for testing condition-specific time trends beyond a shared time trend, per the DESeq2 methodology (PMID 25516281).

acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 is run with test='LRT', full design ~condition+time+condition:time, reduced design ~condition+time, on the filtered DESeqDataSet from T1S1
a results table is produced with gene symbol, baseMean, LRT statistic, p-value and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) for every tested gene
genes are flagged as interaction-significant at padj < 0.05, with the count and proportion of significant genes reported explicitly (not assumed)
results table and the significant-gene list are saved as CSV for downstream steps

steps.name: Per-timepoint condition contrasts and trajectories for interaction hits
caveats: Per-timepoint contrasts are Wald tests on the same model already fit for the LRT; do not refit separate per-timepoint DESeq2 models per subset, which would waste replicates and change the error model.
steps.question: For genes with a significant condition:time interaction, at which time point(s) (t0,t1,t2,t3) does the between-condition difference emerge or change, and in which direction?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 contrast-vector construction from resultsNames; no specific published rule needed beyond the DESeq2 vignette convention.

acceptance_criteria: for each interaction-significant gene from T2S1, the condition-vs-condition log2 fold change is extracted at each of the 4 time points using contrasts built from the fitted full-model coefficients (resultsNames-based numeric contrasts), not re-fit ad hoc
VST-normalized expression means per condition per time point are computed for the hit genes and saved as a long-format trajectory table suitable for plotting
the table reports, per gene, at which timepoint the between-condition difference first becomes non-negligible and its sign, to support later pattern grouping

steps.name: Cluster and visualize condition-specific divergence patterns
caveats: If the number of interaction-significant genes is very small (e.g. under ~20), report that clustering is underpowered/illustrative rather than presenting cluster assignments as robust groupings.
steps.question: Do the treatment-specific (interaction-significant) genes fall into a small number of distinct divergence patterns (e.g. early-onset, late-onset, transient, sustained, or opposite-direction between conditions)?

grounding.reason: No specific published rule for this exploratory step; mclust with BIC-selected K is a standard, defensible unsupervised approach avoiding an arbitrary fixed cluster count.

acceptance_criteria: for each interaction-significant gene, a scaled condition-B-minus-condition-A trajectory across t0..t3 (from T3S1) is computed
genes are grouped by pattern using a model-based clustering method (mclust) with the number of clusters chosen by BIC rather than fixed arbitrarily
a heatmap of hit-gene trajectories (rows = genes annotated by cluster and condition, columns = time points) is produced
an average-trajectory line plot per cluster, per condition, is produced to make each divergence pattern interpretable

steps.name: Pathway over-representation of interaction hits (WikiPathways human)
caveats: Gene symbols in counts.csv must match the WikiPathways GMT's HGNC symbol convention; report any symbols that fail to map rather than silently dropping them.
Do not use the whole WikiPathways-annotated genome as background; using the actually-tested gene set as background avoids inflating significance from genes never eligible to be hits.
steps.question: Are the genes with a significant condition:time interaction over-represented in any curated human biological pathway?

grounding.reason: Standard ORA/hypergeometric enrichment workflow (clusterProfiler) against a curated pathway GMT restricted to a tested-gene background, per clusterProfiler methodology (PMID 39019974, Xu et al. 2024, Nature Protocols).

acceptance_criteria: the WikiPathways human pathway gene-set collection (GMT, HGNC symbols) available in the environment is loaded and pathway names recovered by splitting the descriptor field on '%'

over-representation analysis (hypergeometric test, e.g. clusterProfiler::enricher) is run on the interaction-significant gene list from T2S1, using all genes that passed the T1S1 count filter (the tested universe) as the background — not the whole genome
BH-adjusted enrichment p-values (q-values) are reported for all tested pathways, with the top enriched pathways listed
if the WikiPathways reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports that gap explicitly rather than silently skipping enrichment

steps.name: STRING PPI connectivity of interaction hits with permutation null
caveats: The STRING links file is space-delimited despite the .txt name and ships gzipped with every edge listed twice (once per direction); filter and deduplicate before counting edges.
The full STRING graph (6.9M edges) is too dense for global distance measures; restrict all graph operations to the high-confidence (>=700) induced subgraph on the hit/background gene sets only.

Report the permutation-based p-value alongside the raw edge/hub counts — a nonzero edge count on any gene subset is expected by chance in a dense network and is not evidence of a real module on its own.
steps.question: Is the set of genes with a significant condition:time interaction more physically/functionally interconnected (STRING PPI) than expected by chance?

grounding.reason: STRING v12.0 network construction (id-mapping join, combined_score>=700 high-confidence cut, edge de-duplication) follows the STRING database documentation (Szklarczyk et al. 2023, Nucleic Acids Res, PMID 36370105); the permutation null is added because a naive induced subgraph on any gene list will show nonzero connectivity in a graph this dense.

acceptance_criteria: the STRING human protein info file (mapping STRING ids to gene symbols) is joined to the STRING human links file, restricted to combined_score >= 700 (the conventional high-confidence cut), and de-duplicated for the fact that each edge appears twice
the induced subgraph on the interaction-significant genes from T2S1 (mapped via gene symbol) is built and its edge count, largest connected component size, and top-degree hub genes are reported

an empirical null is built by drawing >=1000 random gene sets of the same size from the T1S1 tested-gene universe, computing the induced-subgraph edge count for each, and reporting an empirical p-value for the observed hit-set edge count against that null
if the STRING reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports that gap explicitly rather than presenting an unsupported network claim

plan.title: Condition x time interaction DE in 2x4 time-course RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw salmon gene counts for 12000 genes x 24 human cell-line samples (2 conditions, time points t0-t3, n=3 per cell, balanced 2x4x3 design, plus one gene-symbol column making 25 columns in counts.csv). The research question - which genes change in a treatment-specific way over time, beyond the shared time trend - is precisely a condition:time interaction test: a gene whose trajectory across t0..t3 differs between the two conditions shows an interaction effect, distinct from a gene that simply moves with time in both conditions (main time effect, the 'shared trend') or that is shifted by a constant offset between conditions (main condition effect). DESeq2's likelihood-ratio test (LRT) comparing a full model ~condition + time + condition:time against a reduced model ~condition + time isolates exactly this term (Love, Huber & Anders 2014, Genome Biology). After identifying interaction-significant genes, per-timepoint condition contrasts characterize when and in which direction the divergence occurs, unsupervised clustering (mclust, BIC-selected) groups genes by divergence pattern (e.g. early- vs late-onset, transient vs sustained, concordant vs opposite direction), WikiPathways over-representation gives functional context, and a STRING high-confidence PPI subnetwork with a permutation null checks whether the hit set is more interconnected than expected by chance, guarding against over-interpreting a naive dense STRING graph.
